'''''Bidens reptans''''' is a [[species]] of scrambling [[perennial]] plant of the [[Neotropical realm]] belonging to the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asteraceae]]<ref name="kew">{{cite web
| url = https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:185190-1
| title = ''Bidens reptans'' G.Don
| website = Plants of the World Online
| location = United Kingdom
| publisher = Royal Botanic Gardens Kew
| access-date = March 1, 2026
}}</ref>

==Description==

''Bidens reptans'' displays these main features:<ref name="vc">{{cite journal
| last1 = Villarreal Q.
| first1 = José
| last2 = Estrada C.
| first2 = Eduardo
| title = Asteraceae Tribu Coreopsideae
| journal = Flora de Veracruz
| volume =206
| pages = 36–41
| publisher = Instituto de Ecología, A.C.
| location = Xalapa, Veracruz, México
| date = December 2024
| language = Spanish
| url = https://libros.inecol.mx/index.php/FV/catalog/book/572
| access-date = March 2, 2026}}</ref>

*It can be a [[Herbaceous plant|herbaceous]], [[perennial]] that creeps along the ground, lies atop other vegetation, and it can climb into trees as a woody [[liana]] developing branches which dangle.
*Leaves arise opposite one another on stems and may be simple with no subdivisions, or have up to 7 [[Leaflet (botany)|leaflets]], which are up to {{cvt|14|cm}} long and {{cvt|12|cm}} wide.
*Flowering heads are all yellow, with each head producing up to 8 petal-like ray florets along the margins, and with an "eye" of up to 30 disk florets with cylindrical corollas.
*The involucre from which the florets emerge consists of two dissimilar series of [[bracts]]; there are 5–8, somewhat fleshy, green, external ones and 8-10 interior ones which are thinner in texture and yellowish green.
*The one-seeded, cypsela-type [[Fruit (plant structure)|fruits]] are up to {{cvt|12|mm|sigfig=1}} long and {{cvt|1.4|mm|sigfig=1}} wide, topped with 2 sharp [[Awn (botany)|awns]], with each awn bearing backward-pointing barbs.

==Distribution==

''Bidens reptans'' is native to the [[Americas]] from [[Mexico]] and the [[Caribbean]] south through [[Central America]]  into South America as far south as [[Argentina]] and [[Bolivia]].<ref name="col">{{cite web
| url = https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/LSHJ
| title = ''Bidens reptans'' (L.) G.Don
| date = February 13, 2026
| website = catalogueoflife.org
| publisher = Catalogue of Life
| access-date = March 2, 2026
}}</ref>

==Habitat==

''Bidens reptans'' occurs in a wide variety of environments, from [[Tropical vegetation|tropical]] [[deciduous]] forest, [[oak forest|oak]] and [[pine-oak forest]], [[Mangrove forest|mangroves]], [[Riparian forest|forests beside water bodies]], [[secondary forest]]s and [[pastures]].<ref name="vc" />

==Taxonomy==

The [[basionym]] for ''Bidens reptans'' is ''Coreopsis reptans'', published in 1759 by [[Linnaeus]]."<ref name="col" />

===A variety in alternative taxonomy===

Sometimes the taxon ''Bidens squarrosa'' var. ''squarrosa'' is listed as a variety of ''Bidens reptans''. This odd situation is recognized as an alternative approach in botanical literature to reflect the two taxons' high degree of similarity and common ancestry.<ref>{{cite journal
| last = Villaseñor
| first = Jose Luis
| title = A New Scandent Species of ''Bidens'' (Asteraceae) from the Balisas River Basin, Mexico 
| journal = Aliso: A Journal of Systematic and Floristic Botany
| volume = 12
| issue = 3
| pages =  579–582
| publisher = California Botanic Garden
| date = 1990
| url = https://scholarship.claremont.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1460&context=aliso#:~:text=Page%202,E.
| access-date = March 3, 2026}}</ref>

===Etymology===

The genus name ''Bidens'' is from the [[Neo-Latin|New Latin]] ''bi'', meaning "two", and ''dens'' meaning "tooth"; so "two-toothed", alluding to the two bristle-like awns atop the original species' cypselae.<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=103917
| title =  Bidens Linnaeus. In Flora of North America North of Mexico (FNA)
| last1 = Strother
| first1 = John L.
| last2 = Weedon
| first2 = Ronald R.
| volume = 21
| location = St. Louis, MO & Harvard University Herbaria, Cambridge, MA, USA
| pages = 184, 185, 205, 206
| publisher = New York and Oxford: Oxford University Press via eFloras.org
| access-date = March 2, 2026
}}</ref>

The species name ''reptans'' comes from the Latin ''reptāre'', meaning "to creep", reflecting the fact that when not climbing the species creeps along the ground.<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://diccionariover.uv.mx/egvadmin/bin/view/enciclopedia/Bidens%20reptans%20var.%20speciosa
| title = Bidens reptans var. speciosa
| language = Spanish
| date = February 11, 2026
| website = uv.mx
| location = Xalapa, Veracruz, México
| publisher =  Instituto de Ecología, A.C. Flora de Veracruz
| access-date = March 2, 2026
}}</ref>
